report.source_text: Direct examination objectified mycelial filaments. The culture after 5 days showed radiated powdery colonies of khaki yellow color (Figure 1). Direct examination of the colony showed terminal and intercalary chlamydospores (Figure 2). Faced with the difficulty of morphological identification, a real-time PCR was performed using the DermaGenius® 2.0 kit (PathoNostics, the Netherlands). Data analysis was performed using the 2nd-derivative and Tm-calling function of the LC480 software (version 1.5.1.62 SP2). This allowed the identification of Epidermophyton floccosum (Figure 3).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 70-year-old patient with diabetes type 2 (on oral antidiabetics) and rheumatoid arthritis (on tocilizumab immunosuppression) presented with fever and painful swelling of the right leg. Physical examination on admission revealed an erythematous, well-demarcated, warm, and tender plaque on the leg, scaly plantar keratoderma, and intertrigo affecting all toe web spaces. Direct microscopic examination of scales showed mycelial filaments. Fungal culture after 5 days demonstrated radiated powdery colonies of khaki yellow color with terminal and intercalary chlamydospores on morphologic examination. Due to morphologic identification difficulty, real-time PCR using the DermaGenius 2.0 kit was performed, which definitively identified Epidermophyton floccosum. The patient was subsequently treated with terbinafine ointment twice daily and amoxicillin-clavulanic acid.
